speaker: Doctor
text: I am ready to begin our consultation. You mentioned experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to start, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any pain or burning during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history. The relief of symptoms with voiding and dyspareunia are concerning, but since NSAIDs provided minimal relief, I am less confident this is a simple urinary tract infection. Have you noticed any blood in your urine, fever, or flank pain? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None.

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis rules out a urinary tract infection. Given the dyspareunia, relief of symptoms with voiding, and sterile urine, I suspect interstitial cystitis/painful bladder syndrome. Have you noticed any urinary urgency, pelvic pressure, or changes in your bowel habits? REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Painful Bladder Syndrome. The combination of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, sterile urine on urinalysis, dyspareunia, and suprapubic pressure in a 40-year-old female is classic for this condition. No further tests are required at this time.
